transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-22 15:00 PT | Duration 60m | Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Silva, Ivy Chen -- Redwood; Priya Desai, Tom Reynolds, Aisha Khan, Rafael Ortiz -- Cobalt Analytics

Summary (auto): quick interactive demo, then feedback sprint and next steps; lots of security questions.

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the hour, we'll do a fast demo, gather feedback, and map next steps. Marco will drive the live demo, i'll cover pricing and pilot flow at the end.
[00:18] Priya: thanks lena, we're focused on inference cost and latency for our clinical AI prototypes. want to hear how Dedicated helps and what private deployment looks like.
[00:30] Marco: great — quick qual q, are you planning low-latency interactive agents or batch embeddings? or both?
[00:36] Aisha: mostly interactive right now, threads of chat w/ contextual doc retrieval, maybe embeddings for search later. latency target sub-200ms tail for 4-8k context.
[00:50] Rafael: security side — we need KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency in eu-west for a pilot. SOC2 is a must.
[01:10] Marco: totally. we support KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated, audit logs via Console, and our SOC2 report is public. i'll share the link after.
[01:26] Tom: curious about throughput — can Dedicated do consistent 100 qps for 1k tokens? what's the cost delta vs hosted?
[01:38] Lena: quick answer: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; hosted is easiest to start but can be more variable on price. we'll send a compare sheet.
[01:50] Marco: ok jumping into the demo — here's a 30s cold start on an open model we ship; watch the streaming tokens and the token billing info in the Console. (background typing/noise)
[02:30] Marco: note — the runtime automatically micro-batches where safe, but you can pin autoscale policies and set a burst cap. also mention of kv cache to speed chat recency.
[03:05] Priya: slight interruption — when you say kv cache, is that client-side or server-managed? we want no raw data leaving our VPC.
[03:18] Marco: good q. for Private/VPC the KV cache sits in the customer subnet; for hosted it's managed but encrypted. i'll follow up with architecture diagram.
[03:45] Aisha: saw a slide online about quantized variants — do you recommend 4-bit for our use case?
[03:55] Marco: depends on accuracy tolerance. for retrieval-augmented chat we often recommend q4 with a quality guard and canary to ensure regen rates stay low.
[04:10] Rafael: on compliance — any customer-running-on-prem option? we have air-gapped setups.
[04:19] Marco: yes, we have an on-prem package; it's heavier operationally but supports air-gapped requirements. recommend a short pilot to validate perf.
[04:38] (background: someone juggling a call)
[05:00] Marco: demo: sending a tool-calling request to a backend and showing function args streaming back — this is how you integrate structured data.
[06:05] Priya: that's helpful. can you also show fallback behavior when a preferred model is out of capacity?
[06:20] Marco: yeah — watch this: policy routes to cheaper variant or to a compatible hosted model with a graceful downgrade note in the response. we log the fallback in Console.
[06:50] Tom: how do you measure unit economics per route? we need per-team cost center breakdown.
[07:02] Ivy: Console exposes token-level breakdown by token type, model, and route; you can segment by token tags tied to API keys.
[07:20] Tom: nice. what's retention on traces? we need 90 days for pilot.
[07:28] Ivy: default is 30, enterprise add-on for 90+. we'll note that in the follow-up.
[07:45] (brief crosstalk)
[09:00] Marco: moving to a perf demo — running a synthetic burst, showing p95/p99 latency graphs. small transcription glitch: sometimes 'p99' read as 'p nine nine'.
[09:40] Priya: our main concern is tail latency at 4k tokens. do you optimize kernels by seq length?
[09:50] Marco: yes, runtime selects kernels by architecture and common seq lengths, plus it can precompile for your model. there's also sharded KV cache improvements.
[10:05] Priya: can you share a split of latency vs cost for q4 vs fp16?
[10:12] Lena: we'll include a sample cost/latency matrix post-call.
[10:18] Rafael: security again — do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for Console?
[10:24] Ivy: yes, SAML, SCIM user provisioning, and role-based permissions. audit logs show token use and config changes.
[10:40] Tom: about benchmarks — do you run tests inside our VPC or do we run agents benching your hosted endpoint?
[10:50] Marco: both possible. preferred is a short local agent inside your VPC to hit Dedicated/Private to capture real network overhead. we'll provide an agent that emits metrics to your Prom.
[11:10] (silence, note taking)
[12:00] Marco: quick qual on timeline — when would you want pilot to start?
[12:05] Priya: target is September production for a subset; pilot in August to validate latency and accuracy.
[12:15] Marco: good, that fits our pilot cadence. we'll scope a 4-week pilot with 2 weeks of bench + 2 weeks live.
[12:30] Aisha: acceptance — what are the success criteria? p95 < 200ms, mean cost per 1k tokens < $X, and regression rate below 2% on a prompt set.
[12:50] Lena: we'll formalize those into the pilot SOW.
[13:05] Priya: competitive question — we looked at Anthropic and OpenAI; why Redwood vs them?
[13:20] Marco: Redwood focuses on serving control: consistent runtime, cost levers like batching and caching, and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. compared to Anthropic you'd be more locked into their infra; with OpenAI hosted you get simplicity but less control over placement and telemetry.
[13:45] Tom: what about Vertex performance? they have tight cloud integration.
[13:52] Marco: Vertex is strong for cloud-native ML ops but less focused on high-throughput optimized inference kernels and unified rollout policies across private on-prem.
[14:10] (someone drops a 'uh' and laughs)
[15:00] Marco: demo note — function calling with structured outputs, we saw a few small parse glitches in the live run (transcript shows 'function name' mis-called as 'funding name'). this is a transcription artifact not product.
[16:20] Ivy: circling back to pilots: we'll need a short security questionnaire; Rafael, can you share the must-have items?
[16:30] Rafael: KMS integration, data-in-transit encryption proofs, SOC2, and data residency controls. plus a runbook for incident response.
[16:45] Lena: we'll attach our SOC2 and security one-pager plus an architecture whitepaper for Private/VPC.
[17:05] Tom: another practical ask — can you show a billing example that maps usage to our cost centers?
[17:15] Ivy: yes, see Console 'cost allocation' feature; we can map API keys to chargeback tags.
[18:00] (short pause)
[18:20] Marco: wrapping demo — quick Q&A.
[18:30] Priya: on model rollouts — how do you do canaries and automatic fallback?
[18:38] Marco: rollouts use per-route policies: percentage canaries, regen-rate monitors, automatic rollback if quality drops. we also support A/B with traffic split.
[19:05] Aisha: if quality regresses with quantized model, can you auto-fallback to fp16?
[19:12] Marco: yes, you can set thresholds to route to fallback model variant; we log the event and flag the prompt for eval.
[19:30] (notes)
[20:00] Lena: ok capture: we'll send pricing, security docs, pilot SOW, and a benchmark plan. Marco will handle technical bench details. Ivy will share success criteria template.
[20:20] Priya: that's perfect. can we get the benchmark window week of Aug 4?
[20:25] Marco: yes, i'll coordinate with Tom for VPC access.
[20:35] Rafael: one more -- data residency: can you pin inference to eu-west region?
[20:42] Marco: yes for Dedicated/Private you can pin region; hosted can route but not guarantee unless in a region subscription.
[20:55] (closing)
[21:10] Lena: thanks all — next steps noted. we'll follow up by Jul 25 with docs and pricing.
[21:30] (meeting ends)

Auto Action Items (transcript): Marco to run bench plan; Lena to send pricing; Ivy to share pilot checklist; Tom to provision VPC access.

End of transcript.
